{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012KDKESMCfTqSQzt4MdLq3m","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport 'reflect-metadata';\n2\t\n3\timport { collaborator, stub } from '@aquaculture/testing';\n4\t\n5\timport { AuditLogService } from '../../../audit/audit-log.service';\n6\timport { Tenant, TenantPlan, TenantStatus } from '../../tenant/entities/tenant.entity';\n7\timport { TenantResolver } from '../../tenant/resolvers/tenant.resolver';\n8\timport { TenantProvisioningCommandService } from '../../tenant/services/tenant-provisioning-command.service';\n9\timport { TenantService } from '../../tenant/services/tenant.service';\n10\timport { AuthResolver } from '../resolvers/auth.resolver';\n11\t\n12\t/**\n13\t * Public-surface contract — SEC-CRITICAL-001 + MT-LOW-001 regression guards.\n14\t *\n15\t * WHY: the 2026-06-10 audit found the public `register` mutation accepted a\n16\t * client-supplied tenantId with zero validation (anonymous cross-tenant\n17\t * account injection), and the public `tenantBySlug` query leaked the internal\n18\t * tenant UUID + lifecycle status — the exact harvest leg feeding the\n19\t * injection. Both were removed. These tests make re-introduction loud:\n20\t * adding the method back fails CI until a deliberate architectural decision\n21\t * (a \"new tenant + first admin\" onboarding saga) replaces it.\n22\t */\n23\tdescribe('Public surface contract (SEC-CRITICAL-001 / MT-LOW-001)', () => {\n24\t  it('AuthResolver does NOT expose a register mutation', () => {\n25\t    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthResolver.prototype, 'register');\n26\t    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n27\t  });\n28\t\n29\t  it('AuthenticationService does NOT expose a register method', async () => {\n30\t    const { AuthenticationService } = await import('../services/authentication.service');\n31\t    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthenticationService.prototype, 'register');\n32\t    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n33\t  });\n34\t\n35\t  it('tenantBySlug implementation returns only name/slug/logoUrl keys', async () => {\n36\t    // The leaky row the resolver must NOT forward: a full tenant entity whose\n37\t    // `id`/`status`/`plan` are exactly the fields MT-LOW-001 removed from the\n38\t    // public payload. `stub<Tenant>` keeps those field names checked against\n39\t    // the real entity, so a rename cannot quietly turn this into a fixture\n40\t    // that proves nothing.\n41\t    const leakyTenant = stub<Tenant>({\n42\t      id: 'internal-uuid-must-not-leak',\n43\t      name: 'Acme Farms',\n44\t      slug: 'acme',\n45\t      logoUrl: null,\n46\t      status: TenantStatus.ACTIVE,\n47\t      plan: TenantPlan.ENTERPRISE,\n48\t    });\n49\t    const resolver = new TenantResolver(\n50\t      collaborator<TenantService>(\n51\t        { findBySlug: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(leakyTenant)) },\n52\t        'TenantService',\n53\t      ),\n54\t      // The audit and command collaborators are unreachable from the public\n55\t      // query; an empty `collaborator` makes any future call to them a named\n56\t      // failure instead of a silent `undefined is not a function`.\n57\t      collaborator<AuditLogService>({}, 'AuditLogService'),\n58\t      collaborator<TenantProvisioningCommandService>({}, 'TenantProvisioningCommandService'),\n59\t    );\n60\t\n61\t    const result = await resolver.tenantBySlug('acme');\n62\t\n63\t    // WHY exact-keys assertion: a future field addition to the public payload\n64\t    // must be a deliberate decision, not an accidental spread. The exact key\n65\t    // set also structurally proves `id` and `status` are absent.\n66\t    expect(Object.keys(result).sort()).toEqual(['logoUrl', 'name', 'slug']);\n67\t  });\n68\t});\n69\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"40144477-b7e8-40be-ae46-1146607ee4e0","uuid":"224a15d1-ef74-4c07-b28e-7240559e2545","timestamp":"2026-09-21T01:00:30.758Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/gharunner/actions-runner/_work/aquaculture_platform/aquaculture_platform/aria-worktrees/req-AIR-aria-evidence-judge-8bd574788fa0/apps/auth-service/src/modules/authentication/__tests__/public-surface-contract.spec.ts","content":"import 'reflect-metadata';\n\nimport { collaborator, stub } from '@aquaculture/testing';\n\nimport { AuditLogService } from '../../../audit/audit-log.service';\nimport { Tenant, TenantPlan, TenantStatus } from '../../tenant/entities/tenant.entity';\nimport { TenantResolver } from '../../tenant/resolvers/tenant.resolver';\nimport { TenantProvisioningCommandService } from '../../tenant/services/tenant-provisioning-command.service';\nimport { TenantService } from '../../tenant/services/tenant.service';\nimport { AuthResolver } from '../resolvers/auth.resolver';\n\n/**\n * Public-surface contract — SEC-CRITICAL-001 + MT-LOW-001 regression guards.\n *\n * WHY: the 2026-06-10 audit found the public `register` mutation accepted a\n * client-supplied tenantId with zero validation (anonymous cross-tenant\n * account injection), and the public `tenantBySlug` query leaked the internal\n * tenant UUID + lifecycle status — the exact harvest leg feeding the\n * injection. Both were removed. These tests make re-introduction loud:\n * adding the method back fails CI until a deliberate architectural decision\n * (a \"new tenant + first admin\" onboarding saga) replaces it.\n */\ndescribe('Public surface contract (SEC-CRITICAL-001 / MT-LOW-001)', () => {\n  it('AuthResolver does NOT expose a register mutation', () => {\n    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthResolver.prototype, 'register');\n    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n\n  it('AuthenticationService does NOT expose a register method', async () => {\n    const { AuthenticationService } = await import('../services/authentication.service');\n    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthenticationService.prototype, 'register');\n    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n\n  it('tenantBySlug implementation returns only name/slug/logoUrl keys', async () => {\n    // The leaky row the resolver must NOT forward: a full tenant entity whose\n    // `id`/`status`/`plan` are exactly the fields MT-LOW-001 removed from the\n    // public payload. `stub<Tenant>` keeps those field names checked against\n    // the real entity, so a rename cannot quietly turn this into a fixture\n    // that proves nothing.\n    const leakyTenant = stub<Tenant>({\n      id: 'internal-uuid-must-not-leak',\n      name: 'Acme Farms',\n      slug: 'acme',\n      logoUrl: null,\n      status: TenantStatus.ACTIVE,\n      plan: TenantPlan.ENTERPRISE,\n    });\n    const resolver = new TenantResolver(\n      collaborator<TenantService>(\n        { findBySlug: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(leakyTenant)) },\n        'TenantService',\n      ),\n      // The audit and command collaborators are unreachable from the public\n      // query; an empty `collaborator` makes any future call to them a named\n      // failure instead of a silent `undefined is not a function`.\n      collaborator<AuditLogService>({}, 'AuditLogService'),\n      collaborator<TenantProvisioningCommandService>({}, 'TenantProvisioningCommandService'),\n    );\n\n    const result = await resolver.tenantBySlug('acme');\n\n    // WHY exact-keys assertion: a future field addition to the public payload\n    // must be a deliberate decision, not an accidental spread. The exact key\n    // set also structurally proves `id` and `status` are absent.\n    expect(Object.keys(result).sort()).toEqual(['logoUrl', 'name', 'slug']);\n  });\n});\n","numLines":69,"startLine":1,"totalLines":69}}}

object) as\n25\t      | RateLimitRouteConfig\n26\t      | undefined;\n27\t  };\n28\t\n29\t  it.each([\n30\t    ['login', 5, 15 * 60_000],\n31\t    ['refreshToken', 10, 5 * 60_000],\n32\t    ['forgotPassword', 3, 60 * 60_000],\n33\t    ['resetPassword', 3, 60 * 60_000],\n34\t  ])('AuthResolver.%s carries @RateLimit(%i / %ims)', (method, limit, windowMs) => {\n35\t    const config = configOf(AuthResolver.prototype, method);\n36\t    expect(config).toBeDefined();\n37\t    expect(config?.limit).toBe(limit);\n38\t    expect(config?.windowMs).toBe(windowMs);\n39\t  });\n40\t\n41\t  it('MfaResolver.verifyMfaLogin carries @RateLimit(5 / 15m) keyed by the challenge token', () => {\n42\t    const config = configOf(MfaResolver.prototype, 'verifyMfaLogin');\n43\t    expect(config).toBeDefined();\n44\t    expect(config?.limit).toBe(5);\n45\t    expect(config?.windowMs).toBe(15 * 60_000);\n46\t    // WHAT the identifier guards: 5 guesses per CHALLENGE, so IP rotation\n47\t    // does not refresh the 6-digit TOTP budget.\n48\t    expect(config?.identifier?.({ args: { input: { mfaToken: 'challenge-1' } } })).toBe(\n49\t      'challenge-1',\n50\t    );\n51\t expect(config?.identifier?.({ args: { input: { email: 'User@X.com' } } })).toBe('user@x.com');\n56\t    // No email in args → dimension skipped (falls back to user/tenant/ip).\n57\t 'reflect-metadata';\n\nimport {\n  RATE_LIMIT_CONFIG_KEY,\n  RateLimitRouteConfig,\n} from '@aquaculture/backend-common/rate-limit';\n\nimport { AuthResolver } from '../resolvers/auth.resolver';\nimport { MfaResolver } from '../resolvers/mfa.resolver';\n\n/**\n * Rate-limit contract — SEC-CRITICAL-002 regression guard.\n *\n * WHY metadata reflection: the audit found 0-byte rate-limit stubs while\n * comments claimed \"rate limited at gateway level\" — a control that exists\n * only in prose. These tests pin the @RateLimit windows on every pre-auth\n * mutation so removing or loosening one fails CI loudly (same pattern as the\n * @Roles guard contracts).\n */\ndescribe('Auth pre-auth surface rate-limit contract (SEC-CRITICAL-002)', () => {\n  const configOf = (prototype: object, method: string): RateLimitRouteConfig | undefined => {\n    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(prototype, method);\n    if (!descriptor?.value) return undefined;\n    return Reflect.getMetadata(RATE_LIMIT_CONFIG_KEY, descriptor.value as object) as\n      | RateLimitRouteConfig\n      | undefined;\n  };\n\n  it.each([\n    ['login', 5, 15 * 60_000],\n    ['refreshToken', 10, 5 * 60_000],\n    ['forgotPassword', 3, 60 * 60_000],\n    ['resetPassword', 3, 60 * 60_000],\n  ])('AuthResolver.%s carries @RateLimit(%i / %ims)', (method, limit, windowMs) => {\n    const config = configOf(AuthResolver.prototype, method);\n    expect(config).toBeDefined();\n    expect(config?.limit).toBe(limit);\n    expect(config?.windowMs).toBe(windowMs);\n  });\n\n  it('MfaResolver.verifyMfaLogin carries @RateLimit(5 / 15m) keyed by the challenge token', () => {\n    const config = configOf(MfaResolver.prototype, 'verifyMfaLogin');\n    expect(config).toBeDefined();\n    expect(config?.limit).toBe(5);\n    expect(config?.windowMs).toBe(15 * 60_000);\n    // WHAT the identifier guards: 5 guesses per CHALLENGE, so IP rotation\n    // does not refresh the 6-digit TOTP budget.\n    expect(config?.identifier?.({ args: { input: { mfaToken: 'challenge-1' } } })).toBe(\n      'challenge-1',\n    );\n  });\n\n  it('login identifier shares one budget per account (case-insensitive email)', () => {\n    const config = configOf(AuthResolver.prototype, 'login');\n    expect(config?.identifier?.({ args: { input: { email: 'User@X.com' } } })).toBe('user@x.com');\n    // No email in args → dimension skipped (falls back to user/tenant/ip).\n    expect(config?.identifier?.({ args: {} })).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n});\n","numLines":60,"startLine":1,"totalLines":60}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BRhZidfL43tv7TPoKovUoq","type":"tool_result","content":"90\t    source_hint: str | None = None,\n91\t    context: str | None = None,\n92\t    target_sha: str | None = None,\n93\t    probe_session: GitProbeSession | None = None,\n94\t) -> EvidenceEnvelope:\n95\t    \"\"\"Grade one evidence ref against the committed tree at ``target_sha``.\n96\t\n97\t    ``probe_session`` is the clock and baseline cache of the DECISION this\n98\t    ref belongs to (`evidence_probe.GitProbeSession`): a caller grading many\n99\t    refs for one submission constructs one session and passes it to every\n100\t    call, so the baseline is resolved once and the whole decision's git\n101\t    probes share one liveness bound. A call without one gets a fresh\n102\t    session — the production bounds, scoped to this ref.\n103\t    \"\"\"\n104\t    session = probe_session if probe_session is not None else GitProbeSession()\n105\t    path_part, line = _split_ref(ref)\n106\t    root = Path.cwd().resolve() if workspace_root is None else Path(workspace_root).resolve()\n107\t    canonical_ref, absolute, validation_errors = _canonicalize(path_part, root)\n108\t    self_output_class = (\n109\t        \"aria_self_output\"\n110\t        if any(canonical_ref.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SELF_OUTPUT_PREFIXES)\n111\t        else None\n112\t    )\n113\t    is_file = absolute.exists() and absolute.is_file()\n114\t    is_dir = absolute.exists() and absolute.is_dir()\n115\t    exists = is_file or is_dir\n116\t    content_hash = _file_sha256(absolute) if is_file else None\n117\t    # The baseline is resolved ONCE per decision (cached on the session):\n118\t    # `None` when the caller threaded no target at all, a readable commit,\n119\t    # or a resolution that says WHY the workspace cannot read it.\n120\t    baseline = _resolve_baseline(root, target_sha, session)\n121\t    resolved_target_sha = (\n122\t        None if baseline is None\n123\t        else (baseline.commit_sha if baseline.readable else baseline.requested)\n124\t    )\n125\t    is_glob = _is_glob(path_part) and not exists\n126\t    glob_match_count: int | None = None\n127\t    # Tri-state outcome of the ONE probe against the committed tree: True\n128\t    # (the tree has exactly this), False (the tree was read and disagrees),\n129\t    # None (the tree could not be read). ``attempted`` separates \"no probe\n130\t    # ran\" from \"the probe ran and could not answer\".\n131\t    verification: bool | None = None\n132\t    attempted = False\n133\t    if not validation_errors and self_output_class is None and not is_glob:\n134\t        if baseline is not None and not baseline.readable and exists:\n135\t            # The baseline probe ran and this workspace cannot read the\n136\t            # commit — `bad object` because the target was never fetched\n137\t            # here, `not a git repository`, or a stall. Nothing about the\n138\t            # path can be compared; a path probe would fail for the SAME\n139\t            # reason and read as the agent's disagreement.\n140\t            attempted = True\n141\t        elif is_file and baseline is not None and baseline.readable:\n142\t            attempted = True\n143\t            verification = _git_blob_matches(\n144\t                root, canonical_ref, baseline.commit_sha, content_hash,\n145\t                session=session,\n146\t            )\n147\t        elif is_dir and baseline is not None and baseline.readable:\n148\t            attempted = True\n149\t            verification = _git_tree_exists(\n150\t                root, canonical_ref, baseline.commit_sha, session=session,\n151\t            )\n152\t    if validation_errors:\n153\t        trust_grade = \"invalid\"\n154\t    elif self_output_class is not None:\n155\t        trust_grade = \"self_output\"\n156\t    elif is_glob:\n157\t        # E5/M1 — grade the glob by its real committed matches.\n158\t        trust_grade, glob_match_count = _glob_repo_verified(\n159\t            root, canonical_ref, baseline, session=session,\n160\t        )\n161\t    elif verification is True:\n162\t        trust_grade = \"repo_verified\"\n163\t    elif attempted and verification is None:\n164\t        # A probe RAN and git did not answer — a stall past its retries, a\n165\t        # binary that could not be spawned, a decision whose probe clock\n166\t        # ran out — or the baseline commit is not readable from this\n167\t        # workspace at all. Nothing was compared, so this cannot wear\n168\t        # ``worktree_candidate``'s name (below): that grade is a statement\n169\t        # about the agent's evidence, and this is a statement about the\n170\t        # host. Without this, the kernel rejects with\n2662\t            # evidence_satisfaction_matrix_must_be_non_empty.\n2663\t            synthesized.append({\n2664\t                \"id\": f\"agent-text-{request_id[-8:]}\",\n2665\t                \"verdict\": \"unverified\",\n2666\t                \"evidence_refs\": [],\n2667\t                \"evidence\": excerpt_short,\n2668\t            })\n2669\t        envelope[\"satisfaction_matrix\"] = synthesized\n2670\t\n2671\t    # Carry through any agent-supplied evidence_refs / details / notes.\n2672\t    for passthrough in (\"evidence_refs\", \"details\", \"notes\", \"plan_content\"):\n2673\t        if passthrough in extracted and extracted[passthrough] is not None:\n2674\t            envelope[passthrough] = extracted[passthrough]\n2675\t    if \"evidence_refs\" not in envelope:\n2676\t        envelope[\"evidence_refs\"] = []\n2677\t\n2678\t    # Embed the raw agent text under details so operators have full\n2679\t    # forensic context post-submission.\n2680\t    details = envelope.get(\"details\")\n2681\t    if not isinstance(details, dict):\n2682\t        details = {}\n2683\t    # D1 (Kapalı Döngü) — FORCE-set, not setdefault: this field is now the\n2684\t    # judge's calibration identity (judgment_bridge reads it as judge_id),\n2685\t    # and a setdefault would let the agent's own payload spoof another\n2686\t    # judge's identity into the per-judge precision ledger.\n2687\t    details[\"agent_subagent_type\"] = subagent_type\n2688\t    # ORPHAN-HIGH-781 — the dispatch-resolved model, same doctrine as\n2689\t    # agent_subagent_type above: FORCE-set from the runtime profile the\n2690\t    # executor resolved at invocation time. 1, -1, -1):\n        ch = text[i]\n        if ch == \"}\":\n            if depth == 0:\n                end_idx = i\n            depth += 1\n        elif ch == \"{\":\n            depth -= 1\n            if depth == 0 and end_idx > 0:\n                candidate = text[i : end_idx + 1]\n                try:\n                    data = json.loads(candidate)\n                except json.JSONDecodeError:\n                    end_idx = -1\n                    continue\n                if isinstance(data, dict):\n                    return data\n    return None\n\n\ndef _build_envelope_from_claude_output(\n    *,\n    raw_stdout: str,\n    request_id: str,\n    claim_id: str,\n    agent_id: str,\n    role: str,\n    subagent_type: str,\n    must_satisfy: list[dict[str, Any]],\n    dispatch_model: str | None = None,\n    usage: dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n    confidence_source: str = \"self_reported\",\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Convert ``claude -p stream-json`` JSONL into a kernel-valid envelope.\n\n    ``confidence_source`` is the ROUTE's word on where a judge's confidence\n    came from (typed-judgment plan, ARIA-HIGH-167): every CLI and chat\n    completion in the fleet reports the model's own number\n    (``self_reported``); a typed decision transport that returns\n    probabilities natively stamps ``provider_reported``. Stamped\n    unconditionally, like the dispatch model: the bridge reads the stamp and\n    ignores any spelling the model wrote inside its payload.\n\n    ``usage`` is the run result's own usage block when the caller holds one\n    (ARIA-HIGH-161): the Z.ai transport reports usage on the result, not as\n    a stream-json event, so parsing ``raw_stdout`` alone left the\n    cross-vendor rung's envelope without ``claude_cli_usage`` and the native\n    wrapper released a finished verdict as ``usage_unavailable``. The stream\n    parse stays the fallback for a caller that has only the bytes.\n\n    Claude Code emits JSONL events. ARIA keeps those raw events out of\n    artifacts, extracts the final agent message, and injects the\n    lease-bound identity fields that the agent cannot know.\n    \"\"\"\n    events = parse_claude_jsonl(raw_stdout)\n    agent_text = extract_final_message(events)\n    if not agent_text:\n        agent_text = raw_stdout\n    extracted = _extract_envelope_json(agent_text) or {}\n\n    envelope: dict[str, Any] = {\n        \"$schema\": \"aria/agent-response/v1\",\n        \"request_id\": request_id,\n        \"claim_id\": claim_id,\n        \"agent_id\": agent_id,\n        \"role\": role,\n        \"status\": str(extracted.get(\"status\") or \"submitted\"),\n    }\n\n    matrix_in = extracted.get(\"satisfaction_matrix\")\n    if isinstance(matrix_in, list) and matrix_in:\n        envelope[\"satisfaction_matrix\"] = matrix_in\n    else:\n        # Synthesize from must_satisfy so the kernel's non-empty-matrix\n        # check passes — as UNVERIFIED rows (ARIA-AUDIT-024). The agent\n        # being invoked and replying is transport evidence, not a\n        # satisfaction judgment; the verdict belongs to an independent\n        # judge reading this matrix, never to the executor that carried\n        # the reply.\n        synthesized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n        excerpt = (agent_text or \"<agent produced no text>\").strip()\n        excerpt_short = excerpt[:240] + (\"...\" if len(excerpt) > 240 else \"\")\n        if must_satisfy:\n            for item in must_satisfy:\n                if not isinstance(item, dict):\n                    continue\n                cid = item.get(\"id\")\n                if not cid:\n                    continue\n                synthesized.append({\n                    \"id\": cid,\n                    \"verdict\": \"unverified\",\n                    \"evidence_refs\": [],\n                    \"evidence\": excerpt_short,\n                })\n        if not synthesized:\n            # Last-resort single-row matrix; agent_text is the only\n            # truthful evidence. Without this, the kernel rejects with\n            # evidence_satisfaction_matrix_must_be_non_empty.\n            synthesized.append({\n                \"id\": f\"agent-text-{request_id[-8:]}\",\n                \"verdict\": \"unverified\",\n                \"evidence_refs\": [],\n                \"evidence\": excerpt_short,\n            })\n        envelope[\"satisfaction_matrix\"] = synthesized\n\n    # Carry through any agent-supplied evidence_refs / details / notes.\n    for passthrough in (\"evidence_refs\", \"details\", \"notes\", \"plan_content\"):\n        if passthrough in extracted and extracted[passthrough] is not None:\n            envelope[passthrough] = extracted[passthrough]\n    if \"evidence_refs\" not in envelope:\n        envelope[\"evidence_refs\"] = []\n\n    # Embed the raw agent text under details so operators have full\n    # forensic context post-submission.\n    details = envelope.get(\"details\")\n    if not isinstance(details, dict):\n        details = {}\n    # D1 (Kapalı Döngü) — FORCE-set, not setdefault: this field is now the\n    # judge's calibration identity (judgment_bridge reads it as judge_id),\n    # and a setdefault would let the agent's own payload spoof another\n    # judge's identity into the per-judge precision ledger.\n    details[\"agent_subagent_type\"] = subagent_type\n    # ORPHAN-HIGH-781 — the dispatch-resolved model, same doctrine as\n    # agent_subagent_type above: FORCE-set from the runtime profile the\n    # executor resolved at invocation time. \"judgment_group_id\": null,\n      \"rationale\": \"WHAT WAS VERIFIED. The worktree read of auth.resolver.ts matched the pinned excerpt at lines 160-199; line 169 is @Public() stacked on @Mutation(() => AuthPayload) acceptInvitation (170-171). The excerpt alone could not answer the rule's claim, so I read the adapter and the decorator/guard sources it implicitly depends on. The rule fires when a method has a write route decorator, the Public decorator name, no SkipTenantGuard decorator name, and its file is absent from the adapter's allowlist input (security-boundary-adapter.ts:99 builds the allowlist from input, :157 tests file membership, :210 is the firing condition, :217 the message). Mechanically the match is correct; the adapter's own positive fixture is the same shape (security-boundary-adapter.test.ts:49). WHY IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE. First, the tenant-skip signal the rule asks for cannot be missing from a @Public() method in this repository: Public is applyDecorators(SetMetadata(IS_PUBLIC_KEY, true), SetMetadata(SKIP_TENANT_GUARD_KEY, true)) (roles.decorator.ts:154, :157; SkipTenantGuard itself at :142 sets the same key), and TenantGuard.canActivate returns true on IS_PUBLIC_KEY (tenant.guard.ts:112) before it ever reads SKIP_TENANT_GUARD_KEY (:122). Stacking @SkipTenantGuard() onto line 169 would alter no runtime behaviour; the adapter is matching decorator spelling, not the guard contract. Second, the allowlist the message demands is not a repository artifact: it is a per-invocation input and the tool manifest's default_input declares only roots (security-boundary-adapter.tool.json:21-22), so nothing is ever allowlisted and the identical finding is produced for login (auth.resolver.ts:112), refreshToken (:142), forgotPassword (:208) and resetPassword (:233), each of which must be reachable without a session. A finding whose only remedy lives inside the scanner's own configuration describes a rule gap, not a defect at line 169. Third, the endpoint's tenant boundary is server-governed in behaviour, not prose: AcceptInvitationInput exposes token, password, firstName, lastName and no tenant selector (accept-invitation.dto.ts:13, :16); the service resolves the invitation from the token under a pessimistic_write lock (authentication.service.ts:913, :925) and finds the user through preTenantAuthRepository keyed on the invitation token (:951) — the invitation row, never the caller, decides the tenant. The public-surface contract test that pins the removed register mutation (public-surface-contract.spec.ts:24) shows the pre-auth surface is curated by test demand, which is the opposite of an unacknowledged public write. WHAT BREAKS IF THIS IS MISLABELLED. Recording true_positive would teach rule health that every mandatory pre-auth mutation in auth-service is a high-severity boundary defect, so the adapter's precision signal degrades and any genuine unguarded public write is buried under structural noise. DOWNSTREAM SURFACE. security-boundary-adapter rule precision and goldset curation for public_write_endpoint_without_allowlist. RESIDUAL OBSERVATION, DISTINCT FROM THIS RULE'S CLAIM. acceptInvitation carries no @RateLimit and is absent from the pre-auth rate-limit contract that pins login, refreshToken, forgotPassword and resetPassword (rate-limit-contract.spec.ts:29-33); that is a rate-limit gap that merits its own finding under a rate-limit rule, and it is not evidence for the allowlist/tenant-skip claim judged here. CORRECT PATH FOR THE RULE. Make the check tell the truth about this codebase: treat Public as implying tenant-skip, mirroring roles.decorator.ts:154-157, or source the allowlist from a repo-declared file the manifest names, so an unacknowledged public write is detectable without flagging every login-class endpoint.
